name: Japanese Cormorant
rangeDescription: Rocky seacoasts and islands of northeastern asia
description: A large dark cormorant of rocky marine shorelines, rarely recorded inland, unlike similar Great Cormorant, which is widespread inland. Similar to Great, but adult has more extensive white in the throat and in breeding plumage shows green (not bronze) sheen above.

name: Sulawesi Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Mountains of sulawesi including buton (to southeast)
description: A large, long-tailed cuckoo with chocolate-brown upperparts and tail, a contrasting pale gray head, and thickly barred underparts. Juvenile has a black head and whitish underside.

name: Tucuman Amazon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southeastern bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Large, scaly, short-tailed parrot of humid montane forest with mixed Podocarpus and alders (Bosque Tucumano) of southern Bolivia and NW Argentina. Generally scarce and uncommon.

name: Collared Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Eastern france to balkans and ukraine; winters in tropical and southern africa
description: Males are striking black-and-white flycatchers with a conspicuous complete white collar, all dark tail, and white rump. Females can be difficult to separate from other flycatchers but have a large white primary patch on the wing.

name: Sooty Falcon
rangeDescription: Rocky areas of northeastern africa; winters to southern africa and madagascar
description: Slim, long-winged, long-tailed falcon that is built for long-distance migration. Adults are all gray, while juveniles have pale, spotted underparts.

name: Huayco Tinamou
rangeDescription: Andes of northwestern bolivia to northwestern argentina
description: Large, streaky tinamou of upper elevations of the east side of the Andes. The highland version of Red-winged Tinamou, similar in voice and habits.

name: Northern Beardless-Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Southeastern arizona to southern texas, western mexico, and northern costa rica; cozumel
description: Tiny flycatcher found in Mexico and Central America. In the U.S.

name: Wire-crested Thorntail
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to eastern ecuador and northeastern peru
description: Small, compact hummingbird found on the east slope of Andes from central Colombia to central Peru. Male is unmistakable; look for long pointed tail, wirelike crest, short straight bill, and white band across the rump.

name: Ashy-headed Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Humid forest of southwestern sri lanka
description: Medium-sized, rufous babbler with a gray hood, beady pale eye, buff throat patch, and blackish bill and legs. Gregarious, usually encountered within small groups low in the understory, or on the ground, in wet forests of the lowlands and foothills.

name: Brown-and-yellow Marshbird
rangeDescription: Wet pastures of far southern brazil, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Large icterid with a long thin bill. Mostly dark brown with a sharply demarcated yellow belly.

name: Black Honey-buzzard
rangeDescription: New britain (southeastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A distinctive raptor confined to New Britain. Entirely blackish-brown with indistinct dark markings and a beady pale eye.

name: Velvet-purple Coronet
rangeDescription: Western andes of southwestern colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: This medium-sized hummingbird looks all blackish in poor light, but at the right angle, it turns into a dazzling gem with a purple belly and crown, turquoise sides, and greenish wing coverts. Note bright white flashes in the tail.

name: Curl-crested Jay
rangeDescription: South-central brazil to eastern bolivia and far northeastern paraguay
description: Large jay found in savannas, semiopen areas, plantations, and occasionally gardens where it is usually encountered in small noisy groups. Note prominent black crest that curls backwards and a black throat, breast, and back.

name: Black-throated Babbler
rangeDescription: Forest of peninsular thailand, malaya, eastern sumatra, and borneo
description: Like many other babblers, this is a handsome bird but difficult to see well, as it forages in dense vegetation. Bright rufous above and gray below, with a black throat and bright white brow and circular spot at the base of the bill.

name: Chestnut Wattle-eye
rangeDescription: Benin and southwestern nigeria eastward to southeastern sudan, western kenya, and northwestern tanzania, and southward to northwestern angola, democratic republic of the congo, and northwestern zambia
description: A chunky and short-tailed rainforest wattle-eye. Males are black and white with a very broad black breast band.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Bulwer's Pheasant
rangeDescription: Submontane forest of interior borneo
description: Uncommon, medium-sized pheasant. Male is almost unbelievable-looking; an immense fan of a snow-white tail sticks out of a rotund, coal-black body.

name: White-naped Tit
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed semiarid thorn forest of western and southern india
description: The only strongly patterned, black-and-white tit in its range. The upperparts from forehead to tail are glossy black, with a prominent white patch on the lower nape and upper mantle.

name: Puna Teal
rangeDescription: Andes of peru to northwestern argentina and northern chile
description: Handsome and distinctive dabbling duck of the high Andes. Note the black cap, bright pale creamy cheeks, and powder-blue bill.

name: Spectacled Guillemot
rangeDescription: Kamchatka and sea of okhotsk to korea, kuril islands, and northern japan
description: Medium-sized seabird of rocky coasts. Breeding plumage distinctive, with coral-red feet and large white “spectacles” standing out against the otherwise blackish body.

name: Black-headed Parrotbill
rangeDescription: Eastern cambodia and highlands of southern vietnam (southern annam)
description: A large, black-capped parrotbill restricted to southern Annam in Vietnam and adjacent areas of Cambodia. Similar in general shape and color scheme to Gray-headed Parrotbill (no range overlap) but with an indistinct dark cheek patch, warmer coloration, and no bold black stripes on the face.
